'''Ugo Amaldi''' (18 April 1875 – 11 November 1957) was an Italian [[mathematician]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |encyclopedia=[[Treccani]] |title=Ugo Amaldi |language=Italian |url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/ugo-amaldi/ |access-date=2017-12-10 }}</ref> He contributed to the field of [[analytic geometry]] and worked on [[Lie group]]s. His son [[Edoardo Amaldi|Edoardo]] was a physicist.<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1=Rubbia | first1=C. | authorlink=Carlo Rubbia| doi=10.1098/rsbm.1991.0001 | title=Edoardo Amaldi. 5 September 1908 – 5 December 1989 | journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume=37 | pages=2–31| year=1991| doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Biography==
He graduated in [[mathematics]] (21 November 1898) at the [[University of Bologna]] under the guidance of [[S. Pincherle]]. He taught at the [[University of Cagliari]] (1903-1905), [[University of Modena|Modena]] (1905-1919), [[University of Padua|Padova]] (1919-1924), [[Sapienza University of Rome|Roma]] (1924-1950).<ref>{{MacTutor|id=Amaldi|title=Ugo Amaldi|mode=cs1}}</ref>
